# How to talk with me

I can be flexible in methods of communication. If it's an important convo though, or we're just beginning to work together, let's have calls or video meetings so we can get to know each-other better first. I respond well to conversations based on graphic design principles and don't respond as well to conversations about feelings.

#### My strengths as a team member

Getting it done and doing it right is hardwired into my design process. I'm great at focusing in on the project and thoroughly thinking through the solutions hierarchy and design principles. It's very important to me that the task gets completed to highest standards and that I don't impede on any one else's ability to do their job.

#### What I value most at work

I most value having autonomy and trust; making a difference; and adventure and challenge at work. When I have these things, I'm able to perform at my best and go above and beyond because that's when I feel fulfilled by the work.   
  
Thanks a ton for stopping by,   
  
-pat

Howdy, partner! I'm Pat. I have nearly a decade of experience producing high-quality, thoughtful marketing systems and experiences (for both physical and digital things). I've been with agencies for most of my career, serving commercial and government clients; ergo Webflow is my first time w/ a real deal start up. <(∙.∙<)(>∙.∙)>. With that industry change in mind, I'm learning new ways of teaming, designing, and building. During my first year with the brand team I was open to all of the new experiences being at a start-up had to offer. I said yes to all opportunities that came my way, solved problems as best I could, and was, overarchingly, very reactive. The adage 'you don't know what you don't know' comes to mind, particularly in terms of company culture, formalities, and joining a smaller team.  
  
During this second year I'd like to be much more intentional at work and in my working relationships. Now that I've gone through a full calendar year with the team, I feel better prepared to support our big dreams for 2023.

# Communication

# Not all conversations are the same. I've found these paths have worked best for me when collaborating.

Note :

**_I can be really flexible when it comes to communication styles and am more than happy to find a middle ground that works for both of us! Let's have the conversation if any of the below are uncomfortable for you.  
‍_**

Daily/project communication:

**Short-term teaming:** If we're working together on a single ticket with a quick turnaround, I'm happy to keep communication touch-and-go on Slack or text. So long as we respect the project management processes the design team have in place regarding feedback, dependancies, and ticketing.  
‍  
‍**Long-term teaming:** If we're working together for the first time, or we don't work together on a regular basis, I'd love to spend time together over Zoom, huddles, or voice calls at first. Personally, I find higher bandwidth touchpoints like these helpful to get familiar with your communication style and to set a baseline for interpreting written back and forth later.   
  
I do best learning and have deeper comprehension from a mix of person-to-person communication and focus time with the problem space and materials. Once I feel like I have a grasp of the problem, I like to test my knowledge by producing a round one and then sharing work, inviting other perspectives.  
  
As I designer, I operate via objective measures of success. I often ask myself does a design objectively do its job, is the information design decisions communicating level of importance in order of first most important, second most important, etc. I respond well to conversations based on graphic design principles and don't respond as well to conversations about feelings _(see Introduction: Meyers Briggs, ISTJ)._  
  
I really like using Loom. Using Loom, I'm able to articulate the thought or concepts which go into design decisions. We can also eliminate meetings while making efficient progress and have focused conversations using timestamps or comments on the Loom itself.   
  
‍

Important conversations:

We can connect however for these, just let me know that you'd classify the convo as important for our work or team.  
  
‍

Feedback:

I like to receive feedback and am happy to have honest conversations.  
  
I will rarely understand exactly how I or others feel in the moment. Often my feelings, thoughts, or ideas will get more clear over some time.  
‍  
If there's something that requires an in-person discussion, let's get time on the calendar soon and DM me to give me some context as to what we’ll be discussing so I can prepare some thoughts ahead of time.   
‍  
I get anxiety if there's more than a couple hours between awareness of a problem and the conversation about that problem. I know some folks like plenty of time to prepare, but I'd like to have the conversation quickly to start processing and ammending _(see Working Style: Strengths, Problem Solver)._

Disclaimer :

I don't love condescending language (or language perceived as such). I'd ask that you avoid addressing me with words like 'buddy' or 'bud.'

# Working style

# My top five strengths and some things I'm working on.

I used the High5 Strengths test to arrive at these categories and believe that they do a good job summarizing and ranking my strengths. These strengths, though, all exist as extremes. Most of the time they show up as strengths, but they also have opposites that are less than dope. I think these are worth sharing here for awareness, but also as an invitation for conversation as I work to find balance between extremes.

Focus Expert

_Focus Experts enjoy getting a project straight to the finish line rather than changing directions regularly. They focus on one thing at a time and dislike any distractions. Your objective is to focus on what’s most important. To do this, you need something concrete to focus on, so weekly, monthly and annual goals are your biggest allies. You become confused when you don’t have a clear mission, so goals also help you filter out what’s important and what isn’t. You ask yourself daily if what you’re doing is bringing you closer to your destination, and as a result, others see you as an extremely efficient and self-regulated person. Your ability to focus also makes you a very valuable team member — if anyone begins wandering around exploring side avenues, you quickly bring them back to the main road, and straight to the point._  
  
Conversely, this strength can show up as hyper-fixation. Sometimes I can chase an answer or point ad infinitum and lose sight of the bigger picture or the externalities at play. I've also found that this strength shows up in an evaluation of collaboration, idea, opinion, brainstorm in terms of a binary. Meaning that an idea either progresses the team towards the goal or is a distraction that should be identified as such, and addressed when the timing is 'more-right'. I am working on being more self-aware here, accepting ambiguity, more supportive of different ways of working.

Storytelling

_Storytellers are masters of communication. They like to host events, speak in public and be heard. They suffer in situations where they can’t express themselves through words. You are a born storyteller_ _(See Working Style:Looms)_ _and your goal is to communicate a message. Not only is this your natural talent, but it is also a strength that you constantly strive to improve on. You are always searching for the perfect phrase and powerful word combination to attract and capture the audience’s attention. That’s why people love listening to you. For you, presentation and communication are everything. You might have the best idea ever, but it’s the way you present it that makes a real difference. Your strong communication skills, your ability to showcase work to external stakeholders and your knack for inspiring collaborators are an asset to any team._  
  
Conversely, this strength can show up as overcomplicating responses, situations, or solutions. I often use visceral language or include peripheral details which can be distracting or take up unnecessary space. I'm learning to better identify the time and place for telling stories and trying to keep it more simple.

Delivering

_Deliverers follow through on their commitments and appreciate seeing how this builds more trust and respect among others. They feel terrible if promises get broken - both on the receiving and giving side. Your underlying goal is to take responsibility. If anyone is emotionally bound to following through on their promises, it’s you, the Deliverer. Your strong ethical principles don’t allow you to simply write off missteps with excuses and rationalizations. And this holds true no matter how small or large the issue. Your name and reputation depend on you being responsible for your commitments. That’s why people love to have you on their team. You’re the first person they turn to when assigning new responsibilities, because they’re 100% sure that whatever needs to be accomplished will get done._  
  
Conversely, this strength can show up as over-indexing on mistakes and blaming myself for being imperfect. I evaluate every path before choosing one in an effort to protect myself and the team, and feel uncomfortable making decisions I don't fully understand.

Problem Solving

_Problem Solvers love uncovering flaws, diagnosing problems and coming up with solutions. It is difficult for them to simply sweep unresolved issues under the rug and keep going as if everything is fine. Your objective is to solve problems. While breakdowns often demotivate others, they can excite and energize you. When something does not work as it should, you jump at the opportunity to analyze the symptoms, identify what’s wrong and find a solution. In other words, you are great at solving puzzles. Instead of giving up in the face of difficulty, your goal is to restore something to its true glory — this is what makes you particularly special. In a team, everyone knows you as someone who does not shy away from a challenge, but instead actually fixes things back to normal._  
  
Conversely, this strength can show up as being reactive. I'm learning to throttle my instinctual response and choose words more carefully while focusing more on the needs of the other party.

Coaching

_Coaches love discovering the potential in people and supporting others’ personal growth. It’s hard for them to accept when this potential is being wasted. Your goal is to develop people’s potential. You believe that, contrary to what some might think, everybody has the potential for development. No-one has ever reached the ultimate level of excellence — there is always room for growth. It is your personal mission to help others realize and use their potential to experience success. As a result, you always look for ways to facilitate their learning, from challenging their thoughts in a discussion to creating environments that facilitate progress. As a leader, you truly care about the development of your team members, and they respect you for that._

# Team values

# When working with others, here are three characteristics that spark a ton of joy and motivation for me and three that I don't value as much _(not that they are not important)_.

**(3)** Things I value a lot

**Autonomy and trust**

Determining the nature or direction of my work without significant instruction from others helps me to feel more invested in the work and outcomes. I collaborate really well with folks when there is trust between all members of the team. When working with others I mesh well with folks who have their own autonomy and processes in place. I am motivated to do my personal best work when I know the other members of the team don't require a ton of direction.  
‍

**Making a difference**

Having a positive impact on the human race is important to me. Webflow, for example, is an amazing tool that makes life less difficult for humans and that's a huge motivator for me showing up at work everyday. Differently, mentoring and helping others in their careers is another way I show up that doesn't feel like work _(see Working Style, Coaching)._  
‍

**Adventure and challenge**

I'm motivated by exploring and experiencing new things. That could mean creating different workflows, learning a new software, or seeing work live in a new way _(i.e. webflow conf)_.  
‍

**(3)** Things I don't value as much

**Managing others**

I'm not motivated by the idea of increasing my direct/indirect authority over others. I'm more interested in using technical skills as opposed to functional skills. Things like schedule forecasting, timing/planning, resourcing, project management processes, workflows aren't natural interests of mine.   
‍

**Recognition**

Getting positive feedback for work well done is fine. Certainly, it's nice for others to appreciate, but not the reason I'd start a project.   
‍

**Work-life balance​**

I love garphic design.

# 2023 goals

# These goals reflect how I want to evolve as a teammate on the brand team as well as a cross-functional partner for the broader Webflow mission. I totally welcome _(and would love)_ to have conversations with folks about these.

Keep it simple

This is a goal for both my design work and the way I team. There's a ton of noise in life and instead of capturing every single one of those ideas, I'd like to be more confident providing simple answers.

Fine-tune collaboration

I'm super proud of the work our team produced in 2022. The marketing materials, and cross-functional teaming, and Webflow Conf 2022 were a joy to be a part of. The outputs speak to the capability our team has for high quality work. I believe a lynchpin for our team's success is fine-tuning and mastering collaboration both internally and externally.   
  
So for me personally, I'm working on designing and collaborating 'in public'. Throughout my career there have been set points at which I'd be sharing work with my team members, directors, stakeholders, and clients. Today that is no longer the case. Therefore, my workflow, presentation, and feedback processes need to evolve.

Manage work anxiety

Unsurprisingly, Slack is a source of anxiety in my life. It is a metaphor for me 'showing up' at work and I often feel like I have to be aware of my team's conversations at all times in order to do my job. This includes after hours or while on PTO.   
  
I'm still very much developing my virtual professional work practices and personality and evolving, in all ways, as a teammate and communicator. Thanks for your patience and support!

Refine and unlearn certain skills

My toxic trait is that I grew up in the consulting industry-- most recently, a "Creative Consultancy" if you want.I've learned a ton while being there and am thankful for those experiences.   
  
**CONTEXT:**In a past life, I've created and taught design curriculum, helped design and stand up a new studio in Austin, Texas, and been a key personnel as we built out a branding competency for public sector clients at a national scale. I've pitched work to C-suites and corralled rooms of 15+ execs around a color wheel to find the _perfect_ shade of orange.  
  
While working for clients, I learned to get the work done fast. Contracts were being scoped by folks who didn't know about design. Something was always on fire, and the timeline was always unrealistic. I made a name for myself as the team member to resolve the toughest contracts. Because of that, I was rewarded by my studio leads as we were all working against the same systemic issues.   
‍  
These rewards were given in return for soft-skills and brute force. Most of these reinforcements, I've learned over this last year, don't translate to day-to-day life now that I'm on on the Webflow team.  
  
At Webflow, our brand team is super collaborative and structurally very open compared to past teams. We're not working _against_ something, it's not us versus a really tough contract, nor are we operating in what I would, with 80%-seriousness, call a traumatic work environment.  
  
So, I'd like to share some of the ways of working that I'd like to refine or unlearn as we move into 2023.   
  
First, I'd like to refine the urgency and pressure with which I approach most decisions. Being conditioned by a contractually constant state of fight-or-flight, has motivated me to make decisions as fast as possible and measure all other opinions (not with the the same exact end goal in mind) against 'importance' or relevance.This is uncollaborative and not helpful.   
  
Secondly, I'd like to unlearn the leadership I've been showing up with. Over years, I slowly adopted an authoritative leadership style as my own. I've _never_ been the one to say, "I know best, listen to me."and yet some of my actions this last year would lead you to believe I thought I did.

Move to San Francisco, CA

I love the ability to work from home if I want to, but I find myself not wanting to as much anymore. Professionally, I'm craving focus and routine. I believe relocating to be in the same city as my colleagues will be a step in the right direction.

# Mantras

# ❶ The difference between art and design is that design needs to solve a problem.⁠ ❷ Collaboration is opportunity for experimentation. ❸ Vulnerability is required for creativity.⁠ ❹ Set your own goals or someone else will set them for you.⁠ ❺ Action is the best way to eliminate fear or anxiety. ❻ If you’re not embarrassed by who you were twelve months ago you didn’t learn enough. ❼ You will always have problems; spend your time solving the ones you like. ❽ The stuff we call our life's work, will eventually just be a metaphor. ❾ Who am I to not be gorgeous, talented, and fabulous?
